components.css: .ds-score-card { max-width: 460px; background: #fff; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.08); overflow: hidden; font: 14px/1.5 inherit; } .ds-score-hd { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 12px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; background: linear-gradient(90deg,#f7fbf5,#fff); } .ds-score-hd b { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: #2c3138; } .ds-badge { font-size: 12px; background: #e8f5e9; color: #2d6d2d; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 10px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-score-kv { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; align-items: end; padding: 14px 18px; gap: 8px; } .ds-score-kv > div { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; align-items: center; text-align: center; } .ds-kv-cur { align-items: flex-start !important; text-align: left !important; } .ds-score-kv span { color: #9aa3ad; font-size: 12px; } .ds-score-kv b { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; color: #2c3138; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-hl { color: #1f8a4c !important; font-size: 20px !important; }

narrative.overview: HomeProxy is an OpenWrt proxy management plugin, and its interface is a control console first: a person comes here to read status, compare latency and loss, switch a node or a policy group, and leave. The visual system therefore optimizes for scanability, legibility of numbers, and calm restraint. It is not a marketing surface and never performs. Density is high by necessity but the surface stays quiet: whitespace is structural, and color appears only when it carries meaning. The palette is a semantic instrument — green means good, red means fault, amber means caution, blue is LuCI interaction/manual. Neutrals do the structural work: white cards float on wash-gray panels, and a carefully stepped gray text ramp keeps long lists readable. Craft shows up as precision, not ornament.
keyCharacteristics: Semantic-only color: green/red/amber/blue each mean one thing.
Flat surfaces with one soft ambient shadow; 6–8px radii; 10px pill badges.
Number-first hierarchy: values bold and centered, labels muted and small.
LuCI-native: inherits the surrounding theme's fonts and controls.
Restraint over expression — density without noise.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: A color appears only when it encodes state — good, fault, caution, or manual. There is no decorative tint.

rules.name: The Fault Red Rule
rules.body: Fault Red (#d9534f / #e4574c) is forbidden as decoration or accent. It means a failed probe, a degraded node, or a danger action, and nothing else.

rules.name: The Number-First Rule
rules.body: In any metric row, the value is the largest and boldest thing; its label is small and muted. A column of values must scan vertically without reading the labels.

rules.name: The Single-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one ambient shadow exists (0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.08)). Do not add a second elevation, a colored glow, or a hover drop shadow.

dos: Do reserve green for good, red for fault, amber for caution, blue for manual/interaction — one meaning per hue.
Do keep values bold and centered above/below their muted labels so numeric columns scan vertically.
Do keep a single ambient shadow and 6–8px radii; use hairline dividers for separation.
Do set numeric cells to white-space: nowrap and left-align only the node-name column.
Do inherit LuCI theme fonts and form controls so the plugin reads as native router UI.
donts: Don't tint a surface, card, or region unless the tint encodes state — no decorative fills.
Don't use gradients as page or card grounds; the one green-to-white header strip is the only exception.
Don't use large blocks of saturated color or heavy drop shadows; depth is tonal + one soft shadow only.
Don't use Fault Red as an accent or brand color — it means fault and nothing else.
Don't over-weight numbers or add a second elevation on hover; state changes are color + border, not shadow.
